clue.text: After much delay, book of maps is printed on time

blocks.note: an atlas is a book of maps
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A long-awaited atlas finally comes off the press on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is printed on' simply places the book before the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase AT LAST is an exclamation of relief when something finally happens following a long wait.

clue.text: Heartless gibe after one leaves Italian town to get help

indicators.note: when something leaves, it departs, so that letter is taken out of the town's name
without a heart means the central letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: Assisi, the Umbrian hill town of St Francis
the Roman numeral for one, which departs from the town
a taunt is a gibe; its middle letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone stops mocking once a visitor departs an Italian town, in order to get help.
explanation.walkthrough: Assisi is the Umbrian town of St Francis; 'Heartless' removes only the central letter of the gibe.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is a helper, and 'help' is used as a noun for the person who helps, as in hired help.

clue.text: Animal in a shaded avenue, curled up

indicators.note: in a down clue, curling up turns the letters back on themselves so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
a mall is a tree-lined walk or avenue, like The Mall in London

explanation.surface: An animal lies curled up asleep on a shady tree-lined avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MALL read upwards gives LLAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American domesticated animal related to the camel.

clue.text: Boy in news, extremely lucky in resort

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of the following word
to re-sort letters is to sort them again into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
the outside letters of lucky

explanation.surface: A lad makes the headlines after a stroke of fortune at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a seaside town but tells you to sort the letters again.
explanation.definitionFit: Selwyn is a male first name, and crosswords use 'boy' to define any boy's name.

clue.text: Blokes following a copper showing insight

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the blokes are placed behind the other two pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Some men tail a police officer and display real perceptiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the blokes after A and the copper. The copper is the metal here, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen judgement or shrewdness, a close synonym of insight.

clue.text: Pass old high road, in a state

indicators.note: high can mean drunk or intoxicated, so the next word staggers into a muddled order

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is a common abbreviation for old
these four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone traverses an old mountain highway while in quite a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high road' reads as one phrase, but 'high' is the anagram signal for 'road'. 'in a state' looks like 'flustered'; it is really the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the United States, a Rocky Mountain state.

clue.text: Joy could get me payment from tenant across the border

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one word stretches round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
rent is what a tenant pays
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A landlord would be delighted to collect rent from a tenant who lives over the border.
explanation.walkthrough: ME, then RENT placed across RIM: R(RIM)ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment is cheerful fun and laughter, a close synonym of joy.

clue.text: The lowest point in Florida (not written about)

indicators.note: in says the answer is lodged within the following words, across their boundary
written about means set down the other way round, read from right to left

blocks.note: the tail of Florida runs into the first letter of not

explanation.surface: A geography question about the lowest spot in Florida, with a teasing bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside, but 'written about' is the reversal signal and 'not' supplies the final letter of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A nadir is the lowest point of anything, literally the point of the celestial sphere directly underfoot.

clue.text: Rascal wanting ring, last piece of jewellery amongst stolen property

indicators.note: the last piece of a word is its final letter
being amongst something puts it in the middle, enclosed by the other word

blocks.note: swag is slang for loot or stolen goods
to ring is to call on the phone
the final letter of jewellery

explanation.surface: A thief wants a ring, the final item missing from his haul of jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery in this surface but is the phone verb; swag is old slang for a burglar's loot.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rogue, so the word is a playful synonym for a rascal.

clue.text: Intentionally ambiguous statements made by sly person ahead of angry speech

blocks.note: a weasel is a sneaky, sly person
to have words is to argue angrily

explanation.surface: A cunning character issues vague statements before an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angry speech' works because 'to have words' with someone means to quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Weasel words are deliberately evasive phrasings chosen to mislead while seeming to commit to something.

clue.text: Party the go-getter spoiled

indicators.note: something spoiled has been ruined and knocked out of its proper shape

blocks.note: every letter of these words is reworked

explanation.surface: An ambitious high-flyer ruined the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-together is an informal social gathering, which is a kind of party.

clue.text: Sensational cover with ancient city featured inside

indicators.note: featured inside means placed within, so the city sits in the middle of the cover word

blocks.note: a lid is a cover
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A tabloid front cover featuring a lost ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: L(UR)ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes something shockingly vivid or sensationalist, as in lurid tabloid headlines.

clue.text: Dog in time-share, rarely barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazily out of order

blocks.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog seldom barks at a holiday time-share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks like the dog's noise but means mad, as in 'barking mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham terrier is a small white Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Singer in musical (Tommy)

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits within the following words, spanning their boundary

blocks.note: the end of musical joins the start of Tommy

explanation.surface: A performer cast in the rock opera Tommy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is The Who's rock musical, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range below soprano.

clue.text: Mild anger over a note

blocks.note: temper is anger, as in losing one's temper
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A minor flash of annoyance about a note someone left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places TEMPER above A and TE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate weather or behaviour is moderate, without extremes, which is what mild means.

clue.text: An inferior alternative in back next to worst

blocks.note: to second a proposal is to back it
as verbs, to worst and to best both mean to defeat

explanation.surface: A poor substitute, ranked just above the worst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'worst' look like nouns or adjectives but are verbs: support and defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Second best is something accepted because the preferred choice is unavailable, a lesser option.

clue.text: Classified? Start of these military activities on Crete, possibly

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the island's letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of these
ops is short for military operations
the island's five letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query whether wartime operations on a Greek island are hush-hush.
explanation.walkthrough: T + OPS + ECRET. Crete saw major Second World War operations, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-secret describes the highest level of security classification for sensitive information.

clue.text: Mistakes made with underwear

blocks.note: first meaning: blunders, from the informal 'to make a bloomer'
second meaning: loose knee-length knickers

explanation.surface: Errors committed with one's knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British informal for a silly mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means both blunders and old-fashioned women's baggy undergarments.

clue.text: Plant rolled about by the wind in fall? Very small daughter chases it

definitions.text: Plant rolled about by the wind

blocks.note: a tumble is a fall
wee means tiny
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A tiny girl runs after a plant blown across the ground in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chases it' puts the small daughter after the fall. 'fall' also teases the American word for autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbleweed is a plant that dries, breaks off at the root and is blown across open country.

clue.text: Stage favourite's returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, and the apostrophe-S is taken as letters

explanation.surface: A favourite stage show is back.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a stage in a process, as in 'step by step'.

clue.text: A grand in addition

blocks.note: taken as written
swell is old-fashioned slang for excellent or grand

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds more on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As well means also or too, the same as saying in addition.

clue.text: Article reportedly in favour of the nation's journalism

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so these words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: the definite article
in favour of is for, and the nation is the state; said quickly the phrase runs together

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece apparently supporting the country's journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the state's' spoken aloud sounds like 'fourth estate'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is the press, regarded as a power alongside the three traditional estates of the realm.

clue.text: Hidden danger involving male vagrant

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round or including, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a trap is a concealed hazard
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A homeless man is caught up in some unseen peril.
explanation.walkthrough: TRA(M)P.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a person with no home who wanders from place to place, which is a vagrant.

clue.text: Run, avoiding large snake

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping clear of, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a big serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb of escape; it is the noun, a ladder in hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, also called the viper.

clue.text: Having knowledge of a conflict ending in peace

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a war is a conflict
the final letter of peace

explanation.surface: Knowing about a war that concluded with peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware of something is to know about it, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Almost certain to provide yield

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: sure means certain
to render is to provide or give

explanation.surface: Something is nearly guaranteed to give a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yield' looks like output, but it means give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or submit, the verb sense of yield.

clue.text: Submissions — wrestler's third gives delight

indicators.note: third points to the letter in position three of the word

blocks.note: pleas are submissions, as in a court
the third letter of wrestler

explanation.surface: A wrestler's third submission hold thrills the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Submissions' suits wrestling but means pleas made in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them pleasure, so as a verb it matches delight.

clue.text: Girl with drop of table wine

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: Clare is a girl's name
the first letter of table

explanation.surface: A young woman has a small glass of house wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table wine' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'wine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from Bordeaux.
